Wonderful and Weird Things in Our World

Seven lessons of big questions for Year 1. Each week we look closely, ask why, and find out how the world works.

    Week 1

    Why do some animals have strange adaptations?

    Some animals look really strange. Let's find out why!

    The drawing helps us see how it works. These are photos of the real animal.

    Draw your own animal

    Draw an animal. Show the body part that helps it live where it lives. Then label it.

    Colour

    Tool

    Brush

    Hand in

    Big words

    adaptation
    A special part of an animal's body that helps it stay alive.
    habitat
    The place where an animal lives.
    camouflage
    Colours and patterns that help an animal hide.

    Ask at home

    Which strange animal did you like best? What part of its body helps it, and why? Can you think of an animal near us with a body part that helps it?

    What we do this week

    1. Look closely at strange animals and say what we notice.
    2. Work out why each body part helps, using habitat and food.
    3. Move animals to the habitat where they belong and explain why.
    4. Draw, label and colour our own animal on the iPads.
    Week 2

    Camouflage and pattern

    How do animals hide? Look for colours and patterns that repeat.

    We are learning to

    • spot a pattern
    • say what comes next in a sequence
    • follow steps in the right order

    What is camouflage?

    Camouflage is when an animal's colours and patterns look like the place where it lives. It is hard to see! A chameleon is famous for its colours and patterns.

    Choose the background
    Choose the chameleon

    Can you spot it?

    Each photo has an animal hiding. Look closely, then press the button to find it.

    Why do animals do it?

    To stay safe

    Some animals hunt other animals. If a hunter cannot see you, it cannot catch you.

    To sneak up

    Some hunters hide too. Their food does not see them coming.

    Our pattern words

    • patternColours or shapes that repeat again and again.
    • repeatDo the same thing again.
    • sequenceThings in order, one after another.
    • nextWhat comes after.

    What comes next?

    Make your own camouflage

    An algorithm is steps in the right order. Follow these steps with your A4 paper.

    1. Choose three colours.
    2. Make a pattern that repeats across your A4 paper.
    3. Draw a chameleon and cut it out.
    4. Give your chameleon the same pattern.
    5. Stick it on your paper. Can you still see it?
    Week 3

    Why are trees so important?

    Look at our Earth. What do you think the green parts are? Find out what trees do for us.

    Earth with trees

    What can you see?

    Look at our Earth. Most of the land is green. The green is trees, forests and plants. Now press the button to see what happens without them.

    What do trees give us?

    How trees help us breathe

    Press the buttons 1 to 4 and follow the air round and round.

    What happens when forests are cut down?

    Press the buttons to move through time.

    See it in 3D

    Drag the picture to spin the island. Blue bubbles are oxygen. Purple bubbles are air the rabbits breathe out.

    Rainforest games

    Put out fires and plant new trees, or walk, sail and explore the forests of the world.

    Big words

    oxygen
    The part of the air we need to breathe.
    roots
    The parts of a tree under the ground. They hold the soil.
    forest
    A big place full of trees.

    Ask at home

    Can you find three things at home that are made from trees? Look for paper, wood and cardboard.

    Week 6

    How do robots know what to do?

    A robot only does what people tell it. It follows every step exactly, in order. Can you give the robot the right steps?

    Make it with the robot

    Choose what to make. Tap the steps in the right order. Then run the robot.

    Steps. Tap to add.

    The robot's list

      Big words

      instruction
      A step that tells someone or something what to do.
      order
      Which step comes first, next and last.
      algorithm
      A set of clear steps in the right order.

      Ask at home

      Tell a grown up the steps to make toast or to brush your teeth. What would go wrong if you did the steps in the wrong order?

      Week 4
